setup.title: Launch the CloudLab experiment (1 name server + 2 load generators)
commands: python3 cloudlab_api/launch.py launch --name dns-rs620 --num-testers 2 --server-software bind --server-hw rs620 --tester-hw rs620
python3 cloudlab_api/launch.py status <experiment_id>   # node ssh commands

setup.title: On test_host_0: create an SSH key and authorize it on every node
commands: cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub   # append this line to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on NS_Local and test_host_1

setup.title: On test_host_0: generate the zone and load it on the name server
On every load generator: receive replies on one RX queue (kxdpgun in generic mode reads queue 0 only)
Point the search config at this machine
Use the second load generator too (test_host_1, 10.10.1.3)
commands: ssh 10.10.1.3 'sudo ip link set dev enp65s0f0np0 down && sudo ip link set dev enp65s0f0np0 name enp4s0f0np0 && sudo ip link set dev enp4s0f0np0 up'   # same NIC name on both clients

optimize.title: Host changes (run as root on NS_Local)
commands: i=0; for irq in $(grep enp4s0f0np0- /proc/interrupts | grep -v xdp | awk -F: '{print $1}'); do echo $((2*i)) > /proc/irq/$irq/smp_affinity_list; i=$((i+1)); done

rm -f /tmp/samp.log; cat > /tmp/samp.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
end=$((SECONDS+3000))
while [ $SECONDS -lt $end ]; do
  echo "T $(date +%s)"
  grep -E '^cpu' /proc/stat
  grep Udp: /proc/net/snmp | tail -1
  p=$(pgrep -x named)
  [ -n "$p" ] && for t in /proc/$p/task/*; do echo "N $(basename $t) $(cut -d' ' -f14,15,39 $t/stat)"; done
  sleep 5
done
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/samp.sh; setsid nohup /tmp/samp.sh >> /tmp/samp.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &

changes: root: i=0; for irq in $(grep enp4s0f0np0- /proc/interrupts | grep -v xdp | awk -F: '{print $1}'); do echo $((2*i)) > /proc/irq/$irq/smp_affinity_list; i=$((i+1)); done

notes: Lower bound. Two load generators were used, but some higher-rate levels still delivered under 99% of the requested queries, so the load generators may still limit the score. Those measurements are excluded. These are the agent's literal commands. They can include node-specific paths, helper services (samplers, zone-file restore) and a reboot, so read them before running them on another machine.
